items.text: Welcome to the 1.2 Patch Notes, Operators.

[p align="start"]We’re excited for you to dig into the new Campaign Modifiers feature, feature updates, and bug fixes that went live today. Thank you to the community for your continued support and love for the Zero Company crew!

[p align="start"]Developer’s Note: We’ve heard that the community wants the ability to increase the game’s difficulty and start campaigns with additional rules, particularly around Injuries and Permadeath. We’ve prepared a set of new configurable campaign options that can be enabled when starting a new campaign, allowing players to modify key gameplay rules. These include Advantage generation, Injury and death rules, Assist Shots, progression rates, and more.

[p align="start"]These options can be used on any difficulty level, though we recommend playing with the default rules on Normal before applying modifications. For veteran players looking for a more tense and less forgiving experience, these options provide new ways to substantially increase the challenge.
[p align="start"]We’re pleased to offer these options and plan to explore additional configurations in future updates.

[p align="start"]Campaign Modifiers can only be enabled via the Difficulty Settings menu when starting a new campaign on any difficulty. Click the Additional Campaign Options button to see the Campaign Modifiers below:
[p align="start"]Developer’s Note: Any selected Campaign Modifiers will be enabled after you complete the tutorial.

Instant Death: An Operator defeated in a Tactical Mission is permanently killed, regardless of how many Injuries they currently have. Operators injured during Operations in the Galaxy Map are not killed in this manner.

Developer’s Note: While enabled, this option modifies the behavior of the For My Brothers ability, allowing Trick to be downed and injured once during any given mission. When defeated, Trick is injured. If Trick is defeated a second time during the Tactical Mission, Trick will be killed.
Two Strikes: An Operator defeated in a Tactical Mission with one or more Injuries is permanently killed. Operators injured during Operations are not killed in this manner.
Three Strikes: The default rules for Star Wars Zero Company. An Operator defeated in tactical combat with two Injuries is permanently killed.
No Risk of Death: The default rules for Star Wars Zero Company. Operators only die in Tactical Missions when they are injured enough times to be killed under the currently selected death rules.
Static Risk of Death: All Operators have a 20% chance to be permanently killed when defeated in tactical combat. Operators injured during Operations on the Holo-Table do not suffer this risk.

Escalating Risk of Death: All Operators have a 20% chance to be permanently killed when defeated in tactical combat. Additionally, the first time an Operator is defeated in tactical combat and survives, the risk of death permanently increases to 40%, and then to 80% on the second defeat. All further defeats in combat remain at 80% risk. Operators injured during Operations do not suffer this risk, and injuries during Operations do not increase the risk of death.
Standard Health Increases: The default rules for Star Wars Zero Company. Operators gain +1 Maximum Health for every 3 Focus Points they have received.
Reduced Health Increases: All Operators gain +1 Maximum Health for every 6 Focus Points they have received, significantly reducing their natural health gains over the course of the campaign.
No Health Increases: Operators do not receive any Maximum Health increases from Focus Points, dramatically reducing their total health by the end of a campaign.
No Cross Trainings Between Disliked Pairs: While enabled, Operators do not receive Cross Training from Bond Level increases until they reach Bond Level 4.
No Advantage from Area Attacks: While enabled, Area Attacks such as grenades, scatterguns, and flamethrowers do not generate Advantage when damaging enemies.
No Advantage from Assist Attacks: While enabled, Assist Attacks such as backup shots and the Easy Mark ability do not generate Advantage when damaging enemies.
Reduced Advantage from Damage: While enabled, damaging attacks that generate Advantage have only a 50% chance to increase Advantage.
Assist Shots Can Miss: While enabled, assist shots are no longer guaranteed to hit their targets and follow standard ranged attack rules.
Enemies Can Critically Hit: While enabled, all enemy ranged and melee attacks gain a 5% chance to critically hit for +8 damage.
No Perfect Shots: While enabled, all Operator ranged attacks have a maximum chance to hit of 99%.
Locked Talent Respec: While enabled, the player cannot change the talent of any Operator on the roster. All Operators will show the talent as locked in the change specializations interface.

Locked Tactical Respec: While enabled, the player cannot change the primary or secondary specialization of any Operator on the roster. All Operators will show these specializations as locked in the change specializations interface.
Locked Weapon Respec: While enabled, the player cannot change the weapon of any Operator on the roster. All Operators will be unable to confirm weapon changes in the Change Weapon interface.
Developer’s Note: When enabled, Trick will be permitted to change weapons once after his mandatory switch.

Locked Recruitment Refresh: While enabled, the Refresh Recruits button will no longer be available in the recruitment facility. Note that recruits refresh at the beginning of each cycle automatically, and this option does not modify that behavior.
Reduced uses of the Astromech's Self-Repair ability to twice per combat. The amount healed is now equal to the AP spent 30%/45%/60%.
Reduced uses of the Astromech's Built-In Comlink ability to three per turn at maximum rank.

Developer’s Note: While this change is subtle, it stops an interaction that allowed the Astromech to dump the Action Points it granted itself into other units through Built-In Comlink. This combination was particularly disruptive when running multiple Astromechs on the same team. Limiting Built-In Comlink to three uses per turn allows the Astromech to continue granting AP to allies under normal circumstances while limiting the feedback effect from Coordinated Support.

Rebalanced the Scout's Tactical Timing passive progression per tier from 20/‌40/60/80/100 to 30/‌40/50/65/80. Additionally, Scouts no longer gain Advantage from all attacks, only ranged and melee attacks.

Developer’s Note: After observing community gameplay, it became clear that Tactical Timing’s 100% chance to gain ADV on kill was much stronger than intended, especially when paired with various Area Attacks. This interaction needed to be removed to prevent guaranteed Advantage gain of this scale.
Cly’s Electroweb Dart is now limited to 3 uses per turn.
Cly’s Combat Jump is now limited to 1 use per turn.

Developer’s Note: We’ve also made some balance adjustments to Cly's abilities. Her Combat Jump was limited to once per turn to eliminate exploitative strategies caused by the displacement effect of Combat Jump and the excessive mobility it can provide within a single turn. Additionally, ElectroWeb Dart has been limited to three uses per turn. This both reduces the exponential effect from placing huge numbers of darts on enemies and limits some over-the-top tactical combinations that allowed Cly to dominate the battlefield without using the rest of the team to back up her playstyle.

[p align="start"]Developer’s Note: The initial goal of the Upgrade Facility was to encourage interesting strategic decisions around Build Slots. Data gathered after the game’s release showed us that players weren’t engaging deeply with the Upgrade Facility, often because they lacked enough credits to do so. We believe reducing Upgrade Facility costs across the board will make Build Slots more viable, especially once you unlock the ability to research multiple upgrades at once.

notes.title: Note For Players using Minimum Specs

items.text: If you are playing STAR WARS Zero Company on an NVIDIA GTX 10-series or RTX 20-series graphics cards that meet Minimum Specification, adjusting a specific video setting can help improve your overall framerates.
These graphics architectures can encounter additional rendering overhead when processing complex environmental detail.
Open Options and select Graphics.
Find the Environment Geometry Detail option.
Switch Environment Geometry Detail to Off.
Disabling this setting lowers geometry processing overhead, which can assist in stabilizing and improving framerates on these GPU configurations.
